_comment: Positive schema-conformance instances for schema/resource-effect.schema.json. These are ILLUSTRATIONS OF THE SCHEMA, not evidence: no instance here was produced by running anything against real code, and none should be cited as a measurement. Their purpose is to exercise every branch of the schema's conditional rules so that a reviewer can see what each frozen decision permits. Every instance is validated by validate.py.

instances._case: A determined record at the v0 ceiling. catalogue_status frozen permits certainty strong; proven is unreachable by construction (AREF-001 3.7).
A draft catalogue entry caps at heuristic. Note the rule_id carries the -WEAK qualifier the pipeline appended; normalised_rule_id is the catalogue key (AREF-001 D-14).
A blocked entry. The kind is known from the rule, but the scope is not, because it lives in a SQL predicate (B-04). The selector text is the literal statement; nothing parses it.
No catalogue entry at all. The record still exists (AREF-001 D-02, I-03) and says why it is unknown. selector is null because there was nothing to select, not because selection failed.

A Go site. rule_id carries the -GO suffix the detector emits; normalisation strips it into the language field. At the frozen commit effect_for_rule_id returns None for this ID (10-CONTRADICTION-CHECK.md 10.5) - D-14 exists so REI does not inherit that hole.
A structurally unresolvable selector. dynamic is distinct from absent (AREF-001 3.6): no catalogue declaration could have helped here, whereas absent may mean the declaration is wrong.
Internal failure. infer_resource_effect is total (AREF-001 4.1): a crash yields a record, never an exception and never a skipped site.
The declared argument was not present in the call. This is the outcome the draft catalogue predicts for every vendor-keyword-driven SDK, and it is countable rather than wrong (AREF-001 B-03).
